title: A Parish for the Confession
premise: True-crime podcaster Petra Blackwood has built her reputation on closing cases no one else can, so when a fresh corpse surfaces in the decaying parish town of Marrow's End—dressed in clothes stolen from her own closet, wearing the face of a witness declared dead thirty years ago—she can't resist. The victim is tied to the unsolved disappearance of Sister Agnes Doyle, whose confession was never heard before the church burned. As Petra digs, she realizes the 'dead' witness faked their death to escape the parish's most powerful family, and that someone inside the investigation is feeding her just enough truth to keep her hunting—and to make her the next body. In the end, Petra finds the witness alive and hidden in plain sight as the parish archivist; together they expose the family patriarch who killed to bury the confession, and Petra must choose between protecting her source and telling the whole truth on air.
about_author: Ada Okonkwo is a former court reporter who spent a decade transcribing small-town secrets before turning them into fiction. She writes mysteries about people who mistake silence for safety.

chapters.title: The Clothes Make the Corpse
chapters.summary: Petra arrives in Marrow's End to record an episode on the thirty-year-old Sister Agnes disappearance, only to be pulled into a fresh murder scene where the victim wears clothes stolen from her own rental closet. Told partly through her podcast narration, the chapter establishes her obsessive need to close every case. Emotional beat: unease—the hunter realizing she may be the quarry.

chapters.title: A Witness Sworn Dead
chapters.summary: In Detective Ilsa Reyes's POV, we learn the victim's fingerprints match Daniel Voss, the key witness in the Agnes case, officially dead since 1995. Reyes resents the podcaster but needs her archive. Petra interviews the imperious matriarch Camille Ashford, whose family owns half the parish. Emotional beat: the first crack of doubt—everyone lies here, politely.

chapters.title: What the Fire Kept
chapters.summary: Petra explores the ruins of St. Brigid's, where Agnes vanished, and finds a scorched confessional ledger with pages torn out. A flashback-style episode reconstructs the night of the fire. Someone watches her from the treeline. Emotional beat: fascination curdling into fear as the past refuses to stay archived.

chapters.title: The Archivist's Quiet Room
chapters.summary: Petra meets Brother Edwin, the soft-spoken parish archivist, who helps her trace the torn ledger pages while deflecting with unsettling precision. Meanwhile Reyes discovers the victim was killed elsewhere and dressed post-mortem—a message meant for Petra specifically. Emotional beat: belonging; Petra, rootless by choice, feels dangerously at home in Marrow's End.

chapters.title: Loyalty Is a Locked Door
chapters.summary: Camille's son Julian Ashford offers Petra exclusive access to family records—an obvious leash. She accepts, and uncovers that Agnes had been preparing to name a predator within the parish hierarchy. Reyes warns Petra off; they clash, then quietly ally. Emotional beat: temptation—power offered freely is never free.

chapters.title: Dead Man's Voice
chapters.summary: Petra recovers a cassette from the old evidence locker: Agnes's voice, mid-confession, naming initials that point to the Ashford patriarch, Edmund. That night her rental is ransacked and the tape stolen—but she'd already digitized it. Emotional beat: resolve hardening into recklessness; she airs a teaser episode against everyone's advice.

chapters.title: Every Parish Has Its Ghost
chapters.summary: The broadcast detonates the town. Longtime residents turn on each other; Reyes is suspended for leaking evidence; a second body—Julian's fixer—is found posed like Agnes. Petra realizes the killer isn't protecting the past but completing it, staging a ritual only someone present in 1995 could know. Emotional beat: isolation; her invisibility is gone entirely.

chapters.title: The Confession Interrupted
chapters.summary: Following the ledger's numbering system, Petra decodes where Agnes hid the full confession: beneath the confessional floor, moved during restoration—to the archive. She confronts Brother Edwin, who admits he is Daniel Voss, alive, hiding behind vows and dust for thirty years. Emotional beat: vertigo—the witness everyone swore dead has been guiding her all along.

chapters.title: Vespers for the Living
chapters.summary: Edmund Ashford, dying and unrepentant, lures Petra and Edwin to the ruined church to finish what 1995 started. Reyes, defying suspension, arrives as Edmund confesses on Petra's live feed—pride and penance tangled. In the struggle, Camille takes the bullet meant for her father, choosing loyalty over blood at last. Emotional beat: climax—truth spoken aloud at gunpoint.

chapters.title: Statute of Limitations
chapters.summary: In the aftermath, Edmund faces trial, Reyes is reinstated, and Edwin/Voss must decide whether to surface or vanish again. Petra records her final episode and chooses full disclosure, burning her perfect record to tell the messy truth—including her own mistakes. She leaves Marrow's End, no longer invisible, no longer needing to be. Emotional beat: bittersweet release—belonging found, then willingly surrendered.
